text:
Yumi: Heads up, Go client 1.7 introduced route header canonicalization for IPV6 tenant keys. We're seeing console ingestion log noise from the normalization.
Carlos: where in code?
Yumi: go-client/routing/normalize.go, function `CanonicalizeRouteID` now strips brackets and normalizes port blocks. It converts `tenant:[::1]:8080` -> `tenant::1:8080` which collides with existing tenant names that used colons as separators.
Laxmi: console parsing assumes first `:` separates tenant and route. This change introduced collisions in the route-mapping table and caused a dedupe rekey for ~30 tenants.
DevOps: impact: small spikes and some dashboards showing unexpected tenant merges. We rolled back console mapping for affected buckets but we need a plan.
Carlos: rollback looks risky if clients start sending new normalized forms. We need graceful compatibility for both.
Yumi: quick fix in Go: preserve bracket encoding for IPv6 in `CanonicalizeRouteID` (i.e., keep `[::1]`). That preserves uniqueness.
Laxmi: console can add a shim that treats `tenant:` tokens and if it sees `::` sequence, try bracket-aware parse. Also add a tolerant hashing function that includes original raw header as fallback.
DevOps: actionable: Yumi to PR hotfix to go-client; Laxmi to add tolerant parsing in Console ingestion; Carlos to monitor dashboard diffs and prepare rollback plan.
deploy-bot: Hotfix branch `go-route-canonicalize-bracket-preserve` created at 2024-07-03T11:12Z.
Yumi: PR opened with tests that verify old and new formats both produce unique keys.
Carlos: monitoring - added alerts for surges in route key cardinality.
DevOps: thanks, we'll watch the canary.
Laxmi: also adding note to SDK breaking changes checklist: any canonicalization must be backwards-tolerant until console mappings are updated.
